statement: DisMKW (github.com/aplumafreak500/DisMKW) is a pret-style *assembly* disassembly of NTSC-U Mario Kart Wii (RMCE01), not a decompilation. It reproduces byte-identical main.dol/StaticR.rel by assembling hand-written .s with devkitPPC `powerpc-eabi-gcc -O2 -S` + `powerpc-eabi-as` (Makefile lines 4-12 and 220-227). It therefore contains no C source and never invokes MWCC, so it carries zero MWCC frontend/register-allocation information.
evidence: Makefile:4-12 (CC1=powerpc-eabi-gcc, AS=powerpc-eabi-as), Makefile:220-227 (C->.i->.s->.o via devkitPPC), Makefile:10 CC1FLAGS '-O2 -S'; README.md:3 'pret-style disassembly', README.md:6 'Only the NTSC-U version is disassembled'.

statement: The DisMKW StaticR.rel .text section - which is where KartState::updateCollisions lives - is a single opaque blob: `.incbin "baseStaticR.rel", 0xd4, 0x37ef9c` (staticr/text.s). A case-insensitive repo-wide search for updateCollisions / KartState / KartObjectProxy / KartCollide returns nothing except unrelated strings in maindol/rodata.s ('Mario Kart Wii' disc messages, '/rel/RevoKartR.SMAP'). There is no disassembled kart code, symbol, or struct anywhere in the repo.
evidence: staticr/text.s (2 lines, one incbin); maindol/rodata.s:48/60/76/93/237 only matches for 'kart'; grep for updateCollisions|KartState|KartObjectProxy|KartCollide across all 166 files -> 0 hits.

statement: DisMKW has no symbol map and no split definitions. Its disassembler is a vendored copy of pokemontools' generic tools/ppcdisassem.py; functions are auto-labelled `sub_<vaddr>` (e.g. maindol/text_1a940.s starts `sub_1a940: # 0x80021c00`) and tools/configuration.py is leftover pokemontools boilerplate (defaults to baserom.gbc, save-states/). No symbols.txt / dtk config / linker symbol table exists.
evidence: maindol/text_1a940.s:1-3; tools/configuration.py:39-43 (save_state_path, baserom.gbc); tools/ppcdisassem.py (pokemontools disassembler); no *.txt symbol file among the 8 .txt files (all ldscripts + sha1sums.txt).

statement: DisMKW cannot supply source-shape or register-allocation levers for the updateCollisions wall: it targets a different game version (NTSC-U/RMCE01 vs our PAL/RMCP01), uses a different toolchain (GCC/as, not MWCC Wii/0x4201_127), and does not disassemble StaticR at all. The general rule: an assembly-only disassembly byte-matches a binary without reproducing the original compiler's frontend, so it can never inform MWCC vreg-colouring decisions.
evidence: README.md:6 (NTSC-U only); Makefile (devkitPPC GCC); staticr/text.s incbin; sha1sums.txt shows the devkitPPC asm build matches retail NTSC-U bytes without MWCC.

statement: MWCC Wii (0x4201_127) mwcceppc.exe exposes a family of per-function optimizer PRAGMAs, i.e. '#pragma opt_<pass> on|off' (confirmed by the compiler's own diagnostic string: "Increase limit using '#pragma opt_usedef_mem_limit %i'"). The embedded option-name table includes opt_common_subs, opt_loop_invariants, opt_propagation, opt_dead_assignments, opt_dead_code, opt_strength_reduction, opt_strength_reduction_strict, opt_lifetimes, opt_unroll_loops, opt_vectorize_loops, opt_pointer_analysis, opt_scalarize, opt_usedef_mem_limit, opt_defuse_mem_limit, opt_removetailrecursions, opt_rotateloops, opt_optimizenonregaccess, opt_movepostops, opt_findoptimalunrollfactor, plus 'global_optimizer'. These switch individual frontend/optimizer passes on or off for a region of source, which is a different (finer-grained) lever than the command-line '-O4,p'/'~~flag' sweep. The mkwii repo and the whole subagents dataset use pragmas elsewhere (dont_inline, legacy_struct_alignment, dont_reuse_strings, explicit_zero_data, warn_*, suppress_warnings) but contain ZERO occurrence of any '#pragma opt_' / global_optimizer directive.

statement: The residual register wall may be reachable with a per-function optimizer PRAGMA rather than a source-shape edit. Candidate #1: wrap KartState::updateCollisions (or just its head) with '#pragma opt_common_subs off' (+ matching pop/on). Rationale, grounded in the existing evidence: (a) the field notes' confirmed ~14 structural slots / 4-instruction size gap are explicitly CSE-locked ('CSE merges all (u8)playerIdx forms into one clrlwi'); opt_common_subs is the exact pass responsible, so turning it off is the direct control for that gap. (b) The colour wall is a frontend vreg-numbering/coalescing artefact: retail's pe is a long-lived temp numbered ABOVE the rodata pool (so it colours r30 before the pool's r29), while ours is a declared local pinned at v69 BELOW the pool (v88) and therefore always colours r28. Adding/removing CSE'd and copy-propagated temps changes the compiler-temp creation order and count, i.e. the vreg block that decides this order; opt_common_subs off (and, as fallbacks, opt_propagation off / global_optimizer off / opt_lifetimes off / opt_usedef_mem_limit) are the only untried levers that can renumber temps without changing source semantics. Measure by diffing match_percent plus regalloc dump (pe/pool var_r28 vreg ids and colours) for each pragma around the function.
